title: Telemetry Conductor: unify trace hooks and quiet-window anomaly sieve
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Background: We currently have fragmented trace hook implementations across services and an alerts surface that is highly sensitive to short-lived bursts (deploys, warmups). This causes noisy burn-rate pages and a high background of anomaly alerts that drown out real incidents.

Goal: Build a small, centralized "Telemetry Conductor" layer to canonicalize trace attributes at ingest, provide configurable quiet-window / rollout-aware anomaly sieving for burn-rate alerts, and reduce signal cardinality for downstream metrics/log pipelines. Deliver a rollout that is behind a feature flag and ships with dashboards and runbook updates.

Why this matters: Reducing false-positive burn-rate pages improves oncall signal-to-noise, speeds mean time to acknowledge, and reduces escalations for transient deploy events. Canonical trace attributes also speed cross-service SLO reconstruction and root cause attribution for latency/error events.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical trace attribute schema published and implemented in at least three high-volume services (inference-gateway, router, cache-proxy)
Ingestion pipeline adds canonical fields (service_role, model_id, request_path, rollout_tag) and drops two top noisy tags to reduce cardinality by >= 30% in metrics index
Quiet-window anomaly sieve correctly suppresses burn-rate paging for deploy/graceful-warmup windows (configurable per-service) and logs suppression events for audit
Burn-rate alerts preserved for genuine degradation: false-suppression rate < 2% in validation and canary traffic
New Grafana dashboard (telemetry.conductor latency & suppression) created with p99/p50 latency, suppressed_alerts, anomaly_score trend lines
Feature flag gated rollout with canary targeting 10% of traffic and a rollback playbook documented in the runbook
tasks: Write design doc (Confluence) describing canonical schema and quiet-window semantics
Add trace hook shim to SDK (node/python) to emit canonical fields behind feature flag
Enhance ingestion job (kafka->enrichment) to apply schema mapping and cardinality pruning
Implement anomaly sieve service that consumes enriched telemetry and annotates/suppresses alerts
Create Grafana dashboard and link to Console SLO pages
Add e2e test harness: synthetic deploy/warmup signals and traffic storms
Rollout plan: canary -> 10% -> 50% -> global; monitor false suppression and SLI delta
Update oncall runbook and PagerDuty playbooks with new suppression logs and rollback steps
comments: 2026-02-20 Aisha Kumar: Created ticket after weekly observations review — repeated deploy-related pages on inference-gateway (see incident notes: https://go.redwood/incident/2026-02-18). Proposed a lightweight conductor to centralize enrichment and suppression rules.

2026-02-25 Liam Chen: Spike complete. Prototype sampler reduces metric cardinality by ~36% on sampled traffic. Branch: github.com/redwood/telemetry/pull/178. Observed minor tag normalization conflicts with cache-proxy; will adjust schema mapping.

2026-03-01 Maya Patel (PM): Reviewed draft Confluence design and asked for clearer SLI definitions: p99 latency measured at token-emission boundary and 5m error-rate per-model. Added acceptance criteria for false-suppression thresholds.
2026-03-05 Design review (Rafael Ortiz): Suggested "rollout_tag" field and a default quiet-window of 2m for canary deploys. Also recommended suppression audit logs include last_good_trace_id.
2026-03-08 Liam Chen: Enrichment job PR opened (github.com/redwood/telemetry/pull/189). Hook shim implemented for Node SDK but Python SDK needs a tiny refactor — assigned to @Sonia.

2026-03-10 Oncall feedback (2026-03-09 rotation): Suppression decreased pages in staging but we saw one missed alert on high tail-latency during cache-thrashing test — root cause tracked to sampler edge-case. Added follow-up task to tighten anomaly thresholding.

2026-03-12 Aisha Kumar: Marked 'In Progress'. Feature flag created: telemetry.conductor.enabled. Canaries scheduled for 2026-03-18 on non-critical inference pods. Runbook draft located at https://confluence.redwood/telemetry/conductor-runbook
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Unit/integration tests + internal staging deploy (now -> 2026-03-17)
Phase 2: Expand to 50% if false-suppression < 2% and no SLI regression (monitor 72h)
Phase 3: Global rollout and deprecate old suppression heuristics
monitoring_plan: Track suppressed_alerts metric and suppression.audit.log entries
Compare burn-rate alert incidence before/after (7-day rolling) and SLI deltas (p99 latency, error rate)
A/B test on canary vs control to validate <2% missed-alert rate
Alert: spike in un-suppressed burn-rate alerts during canary -> automatic rollback
